It says, I place the chosen stone in the foundations of Zion; and what is the benefit from this? The one believing in him will not be put to shame. Let him stop his tongue from evil. For it is written, death and life are in the hand of the tongue; those controlling it will eat its fruits. If someone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body. The restraint of the tongue is great, just as not having it is a very painful disease. In which also to the spirits in prison, having gone, he preached, who once disobeyed, when the patience of God was waiting, in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, into which few, that is eight, souls were saved through water.

And the Only-Begotten cried out with authority to the souls who suffered similarly, according to the plan of the economy, saying to those in bonds: 'Come out', and to those in darkness: 'Be revealed'. That is, he also preached to those in Hades, so that he might free those who were about to believe, if he had come in the flesh at the time of their life. pass_b_english: The chosen stone is placed in the foundations of Zion, and what is the benefit from this? The one believing in him will not be put to shame, because it is essential to control one's tongue, stopping it from evil, as the Bible says that death and life are in the hand of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21). Those who can control their tongue will eat its fruits, and this restraint is a great virtue, just as not having it is a painful disease. The restraint of the tongue is a crucial aspect of being a perfect person, able to bridle also the whole body, as Scripture says that if someone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body (James 3:2).

The Only-Begotten, with authority, cried out to the souls who suffered similarly, according to the plan of the economy, saying to those in bonds, 'Come out', and to those in darkness, 'Be revealed'. This was his proclamation to those in Hades, that he might free those who were about to believe, if he had come in the flesh at the time of their life, if the incarnation was indeed profitable. For these also certainly recognized him in Hades, whom the gatekeepers of Hades, upon seeing him, were terrified by, and the bronze gates were broken, and the iron bars were shattered.

For the things beyond our economy are beyond nature and tradition, and just as Christ cried out equally to all on earth through his bodily presence, and those who believed were helped, so also through his descent into Hades, he freed those who believed and recognized him from the bonds of death. The souls of those who lived in idolatry and lawless debauchery were unable to see the rays of the divine appearance, and thus they could not faithfully recognize the one who came to free all, who appeared to those below and proclaimed to all in common, showing both his philanthropic and just nature.
